payment_primary_detection.scope: One row per labeled payment. Positive means at least one payment-native deterministic violation; settlement, chargeback and relationship findings are scored in their own scopes.

approved_control_execution.scope: Instance-level (native entity, canonical violation type) over the failure modes an APPROVED control claims. Draft-governed and unregistered modes are excluded — they are blind spots, not execution failures.

adjustments.basis: Strict counts exact name matches only. Adjusted additionally credits findings the engine reports under an equivalent approved name and discounts downstream effects of confirmed findings; every adjustment is itemized below.

planted_anomaly_coverage.scope: All clause-driven planted instances at their native entity; explicit aliases are reported separately.

refund.note: Clause 7.2 obliges the payment's settlement to deduct the refunded principal once, so the obligation is payment-native and the refund is the evidence record. Refund findings are scored under `payment`; no separate refund-native type exists.

relationship_resolution.scope: Settlement-to-bank relationship ground truth; UNRESOLVED is a correct result.

lineage.scope: Persisted production lineage (violations.lineage_type, parent_violation_id, root_violation_id) against the labeled primary/downstream split. Payment-native types only; settlement downstream effects are consequences the label file does not record.

financial_impact.scope: Raw supplied expected_verified_loss compared with runtime attributable leakage; SLA cash delay is reported separately.
financial_impact.scope_warning: The fixture's expected_verified_loss includes payment-level SLA/cash-delay exposure and settlement-level labels, while runtime verified_leakage counts only attributable leakage. The difference is retained instead of being silently normalized.

control_versioning.scope: Every control evaluation must select its version from the target's own transaction timestamp against effective_from/effective_to, never from 'latest approved'.

proposals.title: Domestic Card MDR
proposals.source_excerpt:
4.2  Domestic Card MDR
For domestic Visa, Mastercard and RuPay card payments captured from 1 January 2026 through 31
August 2026, the Merchant Discount Rate is 1.55% of captured payment principal.
   Rate: 1.55% (0.0155).
   Scope: domestic card payments only.
   Fee base: captured payment principal.
   Currency: INR.
   Monetary comparison tolerance: INR 0.01.

proposals.title: GST on Processing Fee
proposals.source_excerpt:
4.3  GST on Processing Fee
GST is charged at 18% of the Approved Processing Fee actually permitted under the effective
commercial term. GST must not be calculated on an unsupported or contractually excessive
processing fee.
   GST rate: 18% (0.18).
   GST base: approved processing fee.
   Monetary comparison tolerance: INR 0.01.

proposals.title: Unlisted Settlement Fees
proposals.source_excerpt:
4.6  Unlisted Settlement Fees
Any settlement deduction not expressly listed in this Agreement or a valid written amendment is
prohibited. The expected amount for an unlisted settlement fee is INR 0.00.

   No miscellaneous platform fee is permitted by default.
   No convenience fee is permitted unless expressly agreed in writing.
   No operational or manual-adjustment fee is permitted merely because it appears in a settlement
    file.
   Tolerance for unlisted fee checks: INR 0.01.

proposals.title: Chargeback Administration Fee
proposals.source_excerpt:
4.7  Chargeback Administration Fee
For each valid chargeback formally raised against a captured payment, the Provider may deduct one
chargeback administration fee of INR 250.00. The fee may be deducted no more than once for the
same chargeback identifier.

   Allowed fee: INR 250.00 per valid chargeback.
   Maximum deductions: one per chargeback identifier.
   Any duplicate chargeback administration fee is not contractually permitted.

proposals.title: Standard Settlement SLA
proposals.source_excerpt:
6.1  Standard Settlement SLA
Each Captured Payment must be included in a settlement no later than T+2 Business Days after its
capture date, unless the payment is subject to a documented hold permitted under this Agreement.
   Clock starts on the capture date.
   Only Business Days are counted.
   The SLA is evaluated at the payment level even when multiple payments are grouped into one
    settlement batch.

proposals.title: Settlement and Bank Arithmetic
proposals.source_excerpt:
6.2  Settlement and Bank Arithmetic
For each settlement batch, the expected net settlement amount is the Gross Settlement Amount less
only approved deductions attributable to the batch.
   Expected Net Settlement = Gross Captured Principal - Approved Processing Fees - GST on
    Approved Processing Fees - Successful Refund Principal - Approved Chargeback Administration
    Fees.
   Unlisted settlement deductions are excluded from the expected calculation.
   The bank credit corresponding to the settlement must equal the expected net settlement within
    INR 0.01.

proposals.title: Refund Principal Integrity
proposals.source_excerpt:
7.2  Refund Principal Integrity
For each successful refund, the Provider may deduct the refund principal exactly once from a
settlement. No separate refund processing fee is permitted under this Agreement.
   Maximum refund-principal deductions: one.
   Refund processing fee: INR 0.00.
   Tolerance: INR 0.01.

proposals.title: Refund Amount Limit
proposals.source_excerpt:
7.3  Refund Amount Limit
The cumulative successful refund principal associated with a payment must not exceed the captured
payment principal unless a separate approved credit adjustment exists.

proposals.title: Replacement of Clause 4.2
proposals.source_excerpt:
A1.2  Replacement of Clause 4.2
For domestic Visa, Mastercard and RuPay card payments captured on or after 1 September 2026, the
Merchant Discount Rate is revised from 1.55% to 1.65% of captured payment principal.
   New rate: 1.65% (0.0165).
   Scope: domestic card payments only.
   Fee base: captured payment principal.
   Currency: INR.
   Monetary comparison tolerance: INR 0.01.
